extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers/referees for American Economic Review: Insights
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for economists serving as anonymous referees for manuscripts submitted to American Economic Review: Insights, covering confidentiality, conflict-of-interest handling, and bases for recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind review / reviewer anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review: Insights are reviewed in a single-blind fashion. Because the referee(s) should remain anonymous to authors, we ask you not to use your name in the body or filename of your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include your name anywhere in the report text or in the filename you upload; maintain anonymity throughout the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for recommendations: robustness, credibility, and publishability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations should not be based on whether potential conflicts of interest exist, but on whether the conclusions in the paper are robust, credible, and worthy of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming a recommendation, focus on whether the paper's conclusions are well-supported (robust), believable given the methods/data (credible), and make a contribution meriting publication (worthy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest handling / disclosure context
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscript submissions are accompanied by individual disclosure statements from each coauthor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that disclosures are provided with submissions, but your recommendation should be driven by the paper's substantive quality rather than merely the existence of potential conflicts. If a conflict materially affects your ability to review impartially, follow journal procedures (e.g., recusal) as provided in ScholarOne or by the editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ScholarOne for submission and review actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEA uses ScholarOne Manuscripts for submission and peer review tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To see more information and instructions for submitting a review, log in and navigate to your Reviewer Center in ScholarOne; follow the system's steps for uploading reports, ratings, and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended external referee guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage you to read the brief set of guidelines on referee reports prepared by Econometrica and the more detailed guidelines published in the Journal of Economic Perspectives by Jonathan Berk, Campbell Harvey, and David Hirshleifer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These external guidelines may be helpful in preparing reports, though they do not represent official AEA policy and are not customized to the conditional acceptance policy of AER: Insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of AER: Insights conditional acceptance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Econometrica and JEP guidelines do not represent official AEA policy and they are not customized to the conditional acceptance policy of AER: Insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that AER: Insights has its own conditional acceptance procedures; tailor your report/recommendation to the journal's policies (consult editorial materials or editors if unclear).
